paper: Gödel Agent: A Self-Referential Agent Framework for Recursively Self-Improvement

notes: The repository exposes final policies and test predictions for DROP, MGSM, MMLU, and GPQA. No Game of 24 trajectory or per-iteration optimizer patch log is present in the inspected tree.
Current src/agent_module.py defaults differ from the published experimental setup (o3 in the updater); use the paper for model/protocol claims.

main_results.title: Four task domains under the paper’s evaluation protocol
main_results.uncertainty: Reported value ± 95% bootstrap confidence interval half-width. These are test-set uncertainty intervals, not standard deviations across optimization runs.
comparability_notes: Gödel-base and baseline task policies use GPT-3.5 in the constrained comparison; GPT-4o performs Gödel Agent’s code improvement. Do not describe the entire system as GPT-3.5-only.
Gödel-free can ask stronger models such as GPT-4o for help; its scores are a separate setting, not a controlled gain from code editing alone.
The paper imports baseline results from Hu et al. (2024). Same execution-model family does not establish identical inference or search compute budgets.
MGSM improves from 53.4 to 64.2, a 10.8 percentage-point gain over Meta Agent Search. MMLU and GPQA improvements are much smaller; do not claim uniformly large or statistically significant gains.

cases.title: Replace an LLM solver with an executable search procedure
cases.provenance: A transition reported in the paper; before/after policies appear in Appendix C.2. No full time-stamped action trace or per-iteration scores is supplied.

sequence.description: Request a step-by-step solution and final expression from an LLM.
The paper reports that the agent tries revisions before changing the computational approach.
Search over number pairs and arithmetic operations, reducing the remaining values recursively until one value equals 24.

reported_result.scope: The reported search-based Game of 24 case study, not the four-task benchmark table.
reported_result.set_size: Not specified in this case-study description.

algorithm.input: Four numbers; each is used exactly once.
steps: Choose an ordered pair of remaining values.
Combine the pair with each permitted arithmetic operation.
Skip division when its denominator is zero.
Replace the pair with its result and recurse.
Accept a terminal value within 1e-6 of 24.
algorithm.source_implementation_note: Listing 6 also iterates initial number permutations. Its displayed return string concatenates intermediate numeric operations rather than maintaining a proper expression tree. A browser reproduction should maintain its own expression tree and be labeled adapted, not identical code.

cases.title: Keep the LLM solver and improve how answers are checked
cases.provenance: One representative recorded progression plotted in Figure 5(a), separate from the search-switch example.
cases.interpretation: Changes can introduce regressions; subsequent feedback can remove a harmful check or recover from a broken output format. The plotted LLM-based run remains below 100%, which is consistent with this being a different trajectory from the search case.
cases.chart_policy: Display the original vector chart with its original axes. Do not fabricate an interpolated trajectory or combine it with the separate 100% claim.

cases.title: Changes also reach the improvement process
cases.provenance: The paper’s Section 6.3 reports these behaviors in prose. The inspected public repository does not provide a complete chronological patch trace supporting an exact before/after replay.
cases.meaning: These edits affect diagnosis and organization of later optimization, beyond editing only the task solver.
cases.demo_guidance: Use source-linked descriptions or explicitly adapted pseudocode; do not present synthetic error messages or invented diffs as recorded agent output.

cases.title: Policies can move between symbolic heuristics and LLM prompting
cases.provenance: Actual policies shown in Appendix E; these are selected snapshots from one optimization run, not a complete trace or proof that every later policy is better.

editorial_recommendations: Lead with a concrete design change: the agent can replace the code that solves a task and the code that proposes the next replacement.
Use the Game of 24 mechanism as the main interactive exhibit: actual arithmetic search, visible expression tree and backtracking, plus source-linked before/after policies.
Follow with the original nonmonotonic curve and explain that it depicts a different run; show what an error and recovery mean operationally.
Make the full constrained result table readable with confidence intervals and metric labels; put unrestricted results in a clearly labeled separate view.
Explain the empirical boundary briefly: small benchmark subsets, costly/fallible validation search, no general guarantee of recursive improvement.

ablation_context.title: What helps self-modification work?
ablation_context.interpretation: The largest drops follow removing planning and error feedback. Removing the initial code-running or LLM-calling tool is different from prohibiting those capabilities forever: the agent can implement basic tools again.
ablation_context.uncertainty: No confidence intervals reported in Table 2.
